title: US inflation remained stubborn last month as Iran war continued to lift prices | CNN Business
text:
Source: CNN

The Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge remained elevated in August, underscoring the persistence of above-normal price increases, new data showed Wednesday.

The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index rose 0.3% from July, bringing the annual rate to 3.4%, unchanged from the month before, according to new data from the Commerce Department.

Inflation picked up on a monthly basis as fuel and other energy prices shot higher as a result of the war in Iran.

Economists were expecting the PCE price index to increase 0.4% from the prior month, with the annual rate holding steady at 3.7%, according to FactSet estimates.

The August report was expected to show some cooling in inflation because of some methodological changes the Commerce Department made to several key categories.

Every year, the Bureau of Economic Analysis updates its massive repository of national, industry and regional data to incorporate newly available statistics and more accurately capture changes in prices.

Economists estimate that the changes could lower the annual PCE inflation rate by a couple of percentage points.

This story is developing and will be updated.
